DBE=1 matches aromatic ring (benzene has DBE=4). But DBE=1 suggests only one double bond or ring. Aromatic ring would give DBE=4. Something inconsistent.

For C7H15O5, DBE = 7 - 15/2 +1 = 7 -7.5 +1 =0.5. Not integer. So formula inconsistent. Maybe there are hetero atoms like O not affect DBE. DBE must be integer, so formula likely wrong.

Add another OH: "CC(C)(C)C(=O)OCC(O)O" maybe. That would have extra O. Count O: carbonyl double (1), carbonyl single (1), ether O (1), OH on CH (1), terminal OH (1) =5. Carbons: same 7. Hydrogens? So CH3 groups 3*3=9 H, central quaternary carbon 0 H, carbonyl carbon 0 H, O-CH2-CH(OH)-CH2OH: CH2 (2 H), CH (1 H), CH2 (2 H). Total H =9+2+1+2=14. Plus maybe OH hydrogens: two OH each have 1 H => +2 =16. So total H =16. Slightly off (need 15). Could be one less H if one OH is deprotonated (O-). But formula includes O5, maybe includes an O-.
